hero.title: Grab × Navier — the black-car network, on the water
hero.subtitle: Southeast Asia's super-app already owns the demand. Water is the only transport surface no one owns yet.
hero.what_we_do_together: We launch a Grab-branded foiling water tier across Southeast Asia's densest coastal and cross-border corridors — booked in-app, premium-priced, region-wide and category-defining. Navier brings the software-defined hydrofoiling fleet and the network playbook now proven in the Maldives; Grab brings the demand, the app, the wallet, and the regional reach. Together we turn slow, weather-exposed ferry crossings into fast, smooth, on-demand water trips — and claim the category before anyone else does.

why_now: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: faster, dramatically more efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent, hybrid-capable with no charging-infrastructure dependency, and autonomy-ready. A ~100-vessel network is already ramping in the Maldives (WSJ/Bloomberg, 2026), and Singapore's regulator is mandating clean harbour craft from 2030. The category gets claimed cluster-by-cluster — and Southeast Asia's cross-border seas are the next surface.
multimodal_fit: Grab already runs the hardest parts: real-time demand, dispatch, dynamic pricing, a trusted wallet, and a driver-partner network. A foiling water tier slots straight in — same app, same wallet, captain-partners instead of driver-partners, the water leg booked door-to-door with the GrabCar to and from the pier. Navier is simply the missing surface in a multimodal map Grab already operates.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. Autonomy is arriving on the water before the road. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.
